column2: req_desc

Owner sign-in.
The owner signs in with the seeded passphrase, landing as published in DP-74, every owner screen and owner API call refuses anyone without that session, and signing out ends every owner session as qualified in DP-87.

Car file.
The owner creates a car file that starts as a draft, holds a normalised registration and private home address, is listed in the owner's garage, and opens on the route published in DP-74.

Gauge readings.
Owner readings are stored per fixed panel as whole microns, and plastic panels refuse a reading and show as not gauged.

Paint bands.
Each panel's paint band is computed on the server against the car's own median on the same substrate, using the thresholds in Business rules.

Units bar.
The units mode bar switches gauge figures between microns and mils everywhere on screen without changing any stored value.

Panel-anchored findings.
A finding is stored as a panel id plus panel-local coordinates, and that one anchor, through the published panel frames, drives the 3D pin, the scene marker, the camera beat, the card and the report diagram.

Keyboard placement.
The owner can place and nudge a finding's pin using only the panel list and arrow keys, with each move announced and the page never scrolling.

Stale edit refusal.
Saving a finding over a newer revision is refused and leaves the newer wording in place.

Build a car file.
An owner can go from sign-in to a draft car with readings, a stored photo and a placed finding in one continuous journey.

Content-judged uploads.
Uploads are judged by their content and published size limit, and renamed, crafted or unsafely named files are refused before they can become a finding photo.

Originals kept as submitted.
Every uploaded photo and invoice stays retrievable byte for byte by the owner alone, and invoices never reach a buyer.

Buyer derivatives.
Every photo a buyer receives is a separate upright copy with no metadata and the owner's plate mask burned in.

Store-confirmed uploads.
An upload is reported as stored only after the object store confirms the object and its hash, and an outage saves nothing.

Record pull.
The owner pulls and re-pulls the car's test history from the roadworthiness-record API, and each pull is kept with its date.

Record failure states.
Not-found, throttled and unreachable replies each give their own status and notice, and the last good pull stays shown.

Odometer tape.
The odometer tape compares readings across recorded units, skips tests with no odometer or an unreadable one, and never reports a unit change as a mileage drop.

Advisory responses.
The owner answers every advisory from the latest pull, and answers carry across re-pulls for the same advisory, as qualified in DP-98.

Publish gate.
Publishing is refused with listed reasons while there are no findings, no pull, a stale pull, an unanswered advisory or a recurred advisory.

All-or-nothing publish.
The frozen version, the rendered report and its stored object land together, or the listing returns to where it was with nothing visible to a buyer and the failure notice held on screen as qualified in Feedback states.

Condition report.
Each version has a stored PDF condition report holding its findings, diagram, readings, tape and advisories, and none of the private fields.

Listing states.
The listing moves only along the legal transitions in Business rules, and each illegal move is refused with the published code.

Publish a car.
An owner can take a draft car through pull, advisory answers and publish to a live listing a buyer can open.

Named links.
The owner issues a named buyer or inspector link for a live car, sees its status in the link list, and keeps its one-time address on screen as qualified in Feedback states.

Ending a link.
A link stops working at once on revocation, on replacement and on server-clock expiry, renewal extends it as qualified in Business rules, and the People table shows time left from the server whatever the device clock says.

Link scope.
A named link reaches only its own car and role, and exposes no other person's name or any owner-only field.

Buyer view.
The buyer's link opens the current version with the stage, cards, panel readings, test record, viewings and offer band, using the masked registration, with the seen count on the stage at 768 pixels and above and in the walkround dock below that.

Hero vertex.
The stage's resting vertex lands on the car's most serious finding, and the paired statements and the asking summary card frame it without covering it.

Panel hand-off.
The stage stays pinned for a fixed scroll distance per finding, and within each beat the camera, rim glow and card travel follow the published scroll fractions and rewind on scrolling back.

Seen records.
The buyer's own forward scrolling across a hand-off writes one dated seen record, and scrolling back or reloading never lowers the seen count.

Read pill.
The I've read this pill on every card writes the same seen record as scrolling in every mode, so the whole walkround works by keyboard.

Still stage.
With reduced motion the stage is a still frame with no scrub and no idle frames, and without WebGL a drawn still replaces the canvas, with the read pills doing the work in both cases.

Touch walkround.
A buyer on a phone gets the same findings and seen records from touch scrolling, and every pill answers a real tap.

Staircase widths.
The finding cards change layout at the published widths, from one column to two offset columns to the three-column offset staircase.

Walk round a car.
A buyer can walk from the top of the stage to the offer band with every finding reached and the count complete.

Viewing slots.
Viewing slots are created, held and displayed in London time on any device, and the published clock-change rules hold whatever zone the device is in.

One slot holder.
Of simultaneous claims on a slot exactly one buyer wins, a repeated claim holds one slot and raises one alert, and a slot frees as qualified in DP-78.

Claim a viewing.
A buyer can claim and release a viewing by keyboard alone from the walkround, in a dialog that keeps Tab inside it, closes on Escape and hands focus on as published, including after a refused claim.

Offer gate.
A buyer can make an offer only on a live listing, with every material finding of the current version seen and no other live offer of their own.

Offer dialog and replay.
The offer dialog completes by keyboard, and a double submit or replay records one offer and one alert.

Offer lapse.
An offer lapses on the server's clock, and the buyer's screen follows the server's status even when the device clock is wrong or a stale tab is still counting down.

Single acceptance.
Only one offer on a car can be accepted, and accepting it closes every other live offer in the same step.

Offer states.
Offers move only along the legal transitions in Business rules, and each illegal move is refused with the published code.

Sale and handover record.
Completing the sale renders and stores one handover record, or leaves the listing under offer if that fails, and of simultaneous completions exactly one succeeds.

Sell the car.
An owner can compare offers with each buyer's progress, accept one through the accept dialog, complete the sale and download the handover record.

Selective re-read.
An amendment clears seen status only for the findings it changes and puts an affected offer into needs re-read until the buyer has read them.

Amendment reaches every surface.
New wording reaches the card, the report and the re-read prompt, the version the buyer saw stays readable, and a removed finding leaves a placeholder.

Agreeing counts.
The buyer's seen count, the owner's per-buyer progress and the open-advisory tally derive from the same records and agree after every amendment.

Signal-free capture.
The inspector's capture screen keeps working and keeps its queue through a reload with no signal, and shows a sync state for each item.

Replayed capture.
A capture batch replayed any number of times applies each item exactly once.

Readings side by side.
Inspector readings and pinned findings appear on the panel beside the owner's, banded against the same median.

Content-free phone alerts.
A viewing claim, a new offer and an offer about to lapse each push one ntfy alert that carries no personal or car detail.

Alert delivery state.
Each alert shows as delivered only after ntfy accepts it, failed alerts stay in the alert list with a retry, and simultaneous retries of one alert from any instances make one send.

Run and health.
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest, reports health, and applies its schema and seed safely on every serve.

Server boundary.
The server refuses oversized, wrong-type and cross-origin requests and never serves source files or credentials.

Seeded start.
A fresh start holds exactly the published seed records, with a live car a buyer can open at once.

Responsive frame.
Every screen fits the three published viewports with no horizontal overflow, with the header, units bar, phone bars and car file link footer behaving as published at each.

Entrances and loops.
Sections enter once with the published timings, nothing animates while idle, the scene draws a frame only on the published changes under every motion setting, and reduced motion removes every entrance.

Stage and buyer page look.
The buyer page carries the dark lit stage, the bright worst fault, the staircase and the hard-edged offer band as described in Visual design.

Working screens look.
Owner and inspector screens, including empty, loading and outage states, carry the same visual language as the stage.

Source integrity.
The source shows real provider calls, a real Three.js scene with its own geometry, credentials read from the environment, and no faked state.

Stage geometry.
Each panel has a published car-space frame, and the stage's view-projection matrix, camera position and camera angle describe the real camera, so a finding's world point can be projected onto the canvas.

Brightest patch.
At scroll 0 the projected hero anchor is the brightest patch of the canvas, as qualified in DP-96 for a closed listing, it is never covered at any published viewport, including when an open tab resizes between them, and it follows the current version in an open tab.

Scene markers.
Each finding has a marker in the scene that shows the server's seen state, as a hollow ring when unseen, filled when seen, and a ring again after an amendment changes it, at the published size on device pixel ratios 1, 2 and 3.

Lost WebGL context.
A WebGL context lost during a walkround drops the stage to the still state with no seen write, and the pills finish the walkround.

Deliberate jumps write nothing.
Links, Next unread, marker taps, focus moves, page opens, reloads, track changes, overlays opening or closing and new versions write no seen record, and a page opens or reloads at scroll 0.

Honest seen count.
The seen count and each card's seen state change only after the server's reply, a failed scroll write is reported and retried, and a finding has one write at a time, as qualified in Feedback states.

Walkround dock.
At 767 pixels and below a fixed walkround dock holds the seen count, the standing line of DP-83 and the control that takes the buyer to the next unread finding or the offer.

Car file bar.
At 767 pixels and below a fixed car file bar holds the listing status word and the Sections button, which opens the car file sections sheet with its standing lines.

Closed and clear.
A closed sheet, menu or accordion row holds nothing focusable or accessible once its exit has ended, and no fixed bar ever covers a focused or tapped control or a focused heading.

Polls leave the page alone.
A poll never closes a dialog or the sections sheet, clears typed input, moves focus or scroll, removes a service notice or the one-time link address, repaints a row with a pending request or draws an idle frame, and only an ended link replaces the page.

Pending controls and focus homes.
A pending control is aria-disabled, keeps focus and sends nothing further, a dialog with a pending request ignores Escape, and focus always lands on the published control or heading.

Lost replies.
A dialog keeps one Idempotency-Key across retries of the same body, so a lost reply on an offer or claim records one offer or claim and one alert, as qualified in DP-90.

Accept dialog.
Accepting an offer goes through a confirmation dialog that names the amount, buyer and offers to be closed, stays current under the poll, shows refusals inside itself, and sends one write however often it is pressed while pending or during its exit, and the Offers table shows the server's time left whatever the device clock says.

Landing routes.
Sign-in, a signed-out deep link and creating a car each land on their published route with the published focus, and a bad return value lands on the garage.

Touch plate mask.
The plate mask is drawn on an upright preview by pointer or touch and applies to the upright image, whatever orientation the photo file stores.

Announced upload.
Storing a photo announces each step as its own update through the status region, including a repeated message, and the stored photo appears in place with no reload.

Live publish blockers.
Publish blockers, the open-advisory tally, their section standing lines and the stage preview's advisory ticks are always shown and always current, updating in place after each save and on the poll.

Revocation reaches open tabs.
Revoking a buyer's link frees their held slot in the same step, leaves their open offer with the owner, and ends their open tab within the poll even with a dialog open, in the 3D stage and the still stage alike.

Amendment reaches open tabs.
Within the poll and without a reload, a buyer's open tab takes an amendment's cards, prompt, count, offer status, scene marker and track length together, writes nothing, and keeps any open offer or version dialog as qualified in Business rules.

Honest capture queue.
A capture row's Synced word changes only after the server's reply, a lost reply returns its rows to the queue, and only one batch is in flight at a time across tabs.

Announced alert retry.
Retrying a failed phone alert, from the alert list or the phone sections sheet, announces each step, repeats a repeated failure, reports a retry already under way, and keeps focus on a real control through any poll.

Section standing lines.
Each car file section link carries a standing line derived on the server, current within the published delay of an action's success copy and on the poll, including while the phone sections sheet is open.

Dock standing line.
The page holds at most one Offer status, which lives in the walkround dock at 767 pixels and below, and with no offer the dock shows the held viewing's label, all within the published dock height.

Stage preview.
The owner's Findings section shows the same scene and camera rule as the buyer stage, resting on the unsaved pin or the working hero, showing one advisory tick per open advisory from server state, and writing nothing.

Lit panel.
At 50% of a beat the current panel's rim is measurably the brightest panel edge on the canvas.

Marker tap.
A click or tap close to a marker's projection goes to that finding and writes nothing, and a touch that moves past the published distance stays a page scroll.

Session ends mid-edit.
An owner action refused for an ended session opens the sign-in dialog, keeps the page and resends the action once after sign-in, and a poll refused the same way changes nothing.

Last photo chosen wins.
The last file chosen owns the preview, the mask fields and the upload, even when an earlier file is still being read.

Unsaved response survives.
An unsaved advisory response stays on its advisory through polls and re-pulls, and a new advisory arrives as a new unanswered row.

Recorded behind the dialog.
After a lost reply, a poll that shows the offer or claim as recorded leaves the dialog open, and the next press replays the key and closes as success.

Replayable acceptance.
Acceptance takes an Idempotency-Key, and a replay returns the stored success before any state refusal.

Shared capture queue.
All tabs of an inspector link share one queue with no lost rows and one batch in flight across tabs, and the inspector places a finding with the panel diagram and pin by a real tap or by keys.

Overlay exits.
A closing overlay is inert at once with focus on its home, its opener reopens it during the exit and it stays open, a scrim tap closes only the Menu and the sections sheet, and opening or closing an overlay on the buyer page at 767 pixels and below moves nothing and draws nothing.

Short viewport.
At 375x480, reached by resizing an open page, a dialog keeps its state and scrolls inside itself so that every control can be reached fully in view, and a focused page field stays above the fixed bars.

Announced poll changes.
A poll-found change the page did not cause is announced once through the screen's status region, waits while a dialog or sheet is open, and then follows that dialog's success copy as separate updates.

Stage follows the listing.
Under offer, sold and withdrawn listings dim the whole scene, markers included, to at most 60% of the live hero patch, and the asking summary shows the status word, within the poll on an open tab.

True still stage.
Each pin in the drawn still lies within 3 CSS pixels of its world point's projection through the stage's published matrix, at every published viewport, after a resize, after a lost context and after a new version moves the hero.

Recurred advisories.
A repaired advisory whose exact text returns at a later test counts as open, is flagged on its row and blocks publishing until its stance changes.
